---
title: "Nets and dn0"
---

A net enters both models as two numbers, `dn0_use`, the probability that a mosquito is killed when
it contacts a treated net, and `itn_use`, the share of the population sleeping under one. Which
insecticide the net carries, and how resistant the local mosquitoes have become, is compressed
entirely into `dn0_use`. `calculate_dn0` does that compression. It is the first call in almost
every `estimint` workflow.

## Net types

Four formulations are modelled. `net_types` returns their canonical names alphabetically, which
puts `ppf` before `pyrrole`.

```{python}
from estimint import net_types, calculate_dn0

net_types()
```

Each formulation has a short alias, accepted anywhere a net type is, and the aliases double as the
keyword-argument names in the wider API.

| Alias | Canonical name | Formulation |
|---|---|---|
| `py_only` | `pyrethroid_only` | Pyrethroid alone |
| `py_pbo` | `pyrethroid_pbo` | Pyrethroid with PBO |
| `py_ppf` | `pyrethroid_ppf` | Pyrethroid with pyriproxyfen |
| `py_pyrrole` | `pyrethroid_pyrrole` | Pyrethroid with chlorfenapyr |

Both spellings are case-insensitive. The canonical names are joined with `_` throughout, so a
hyphen raises `ValueError: unknown net type`.

## From a net mix to dn0

`calculate_dn0` takes a resistance level and the net mix as keyword arguments, one keyword per net
type, one value per share of the population using it.

```{python}
net = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.70)
net
```

What comes back is a `DN0Result`, a named tuple of exactly two fields, which unpacks by position
and reaches the same two values by attribute.

```{python}
net.dn0, net.itn_use
```

At 30% pyrethroid resistance a pyrethroid-only net kills about 31% of the mosquitoes that contact
it. Coverage is 70%.

Passing more than one keyword gives a mix, so that here 40% of the population has pyrethroid-only
nets, 30% has PBO nets, and the remaining 30% has no net at all.

```{python}
mix = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.40, py_pbo=0.30)
mix
```

## dn0 and itn_use

The two fields are built differently, one as an average and one as a total.

`dn0` is the **usage-weighted average** of the per-net-type `dn0` values across the mix, and the
weights are normalised over the nets in the mix rather than over the population. That makes it a
property of the nets that exist rather than of how many people own them, so a mix covering 70% of
the population has the same `dn0` as one covering 20% in the same proportions. Reconstruct it by
hand.

```{python}
only = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=1.0).dn0
pbo = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_pbo=1.0).dn0

by_hand = (0.40 * only + 0.30 * pbo) / (0.40 + 0.30)
round(by_hand, 5), round(mix.dn0, 5)
```

`itn_use` is the **sum** of the shares, 0.40 + 0.30 = 0.70, and it is the total ITN coverage of the
population. It is already complete.

::: {.callout-warning}
## A note on `itn_use`

`DN0Result.itn_use` is the finished coverage figure, not a weight awaiting a coverage term.
Multiplying it by a usage fraction a second time understates the coverage. The error is silent.

```{python}
net = calculate_dn0(0.30, py_only=0.70)

net.itn_use, round(net.itn_use * 0.70, 3)  # the second value is the mistake
```

The model then reads a district with 49% net coverage rather than 70%, and understates the EIR the
setting is judged to need. The size of that error is measured in
[Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd).
:::

## Resistance and dn0

Holding usage at 1.0 for one formulation at a time isolates its resistance response.

```{python}
import pandas as pd

levels = [0.0, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.0]

table = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        f"{r:.2f}": [calculate_dn0(r, **{nt: 1.0}).dn0 for nt in net_types()]
        for r in levels
    },
    index=net_types(),
).round(4)
table.index.name = "net type"
table
```

Read across a row for the decay of one formulation, and down a column to compare formulations at a
fixed resistance. A pyrethroid-only net falls to zero at full resistance. The other three retain
some lethality across the whole range.

Pyrrole nets are the most lethal and the flattest, losing about a tenth of their `dn0` between
resistance 0.0 and 0.75, where a pyrethroid-only net loses nearly a third. PPF nets sit low
throughout the table. Their effect on the next generation is not represented in `dn0` at all, and
reaches the emulator through the `lsm` term instead. The curves come from the same source
`malariasimulation` uses.

## Caveats

`dn0` summarises the kill on contact and nothing else. It captures neither repellence nor the loss
of a net to wear and disuse over a campaign, and one net mix is assumed to hold across the whole
population. The resistance level supplied should be the local pyrethroid resistance at the decision
point, and because the curves steepen above 0.75, vary it in a sensitivity check.

## See also

The two numbers `calculate_dn0` returns feed the inversion set out in
[Estimating EIR from prevalence](estimating-eir.qmd), which also measures how far a double-counted
`itn_use` drags the inferred EIR down. Please see
[Interventions and nets](../03-concepts/interventions.qmd) for the epidemiology behind the four
formulations.
